title: A claude -p timeout in a pool kb or web run is one failed run, not a lost chunk
goal: bench_pool's kb and web runners catch agent_bench.execute's TimeoutExpired and record the run as an error, as the router and hook runners do, so run_tasks writes the chunk's cells and rows; today the exception is re-raised at run_tasks and the chunk writes no rows. Found by the SP-hm4qgf3t review (no chunk hit it).

run: import sys,types,subprocess,tempfile,pathlib; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import bench_pool, agent_bench; agent_bench.execute=lambda *a,**k: (_ for _ in ()).throw(subprocess.TimeoutExpired('claude',900)); bench_pool.spent_run=lambda r: None; run=bench_pool.live_runner(types.SimpleNamespace(lookup=lambda: '.', scratch=pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())),'sh'); r=run('haiku-5-5','default',{'question':'q'}); assert 'error' in r, r

notes: Blocks the next pool benchmark record: the operator asked on 2026-10-08 for the work needed before the next record to be staged as SP-2vhfsn4o.
